name: 10-epi-γ-Eudesmol

pubchem.title: 10-epi-gamma-Eudesmol
pubchem.description: 10-epi-gamma-eudesmol is a eudesmane sesquiterpenoid in which the eudesmane skeleton carries a hydroxy substituent at C-11, has a double bond between C-4 and C-5 and has inversion of configuration at C-10. It has a role as a volatile oil component.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: 10-epi-gamma-Eudesmol is a sesquiterpenoid, a type of aromatic molecule found in the volatile essential oils of various plants. As a component of these fragrant oils, it contributes to the complex scents and botanical defenses of the plants that produce it. You might encounter it in the aroma of certain herbs, spices, and even some varieties of cannabis.
consumer_summary.found_in: This molecule is found in the essential oils of familiar aromatic plants like clary sage, sweet wormwood, and geraniums. It has also been identified in the volatile profiles of certain cannabis strains and members of the ginger family.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to 10-epi-gamma-Eudesmol for its potential as an active botanical defense compound, particularly exploring its ability to fight off microbes and oxidative stress. The scientific community is investigating whether this fragrant molecule could serve as a natural anti-infective or anti-inflammatory agent. The strongest evidence so far comes from early animal research (Oxford level 5), which is laying the groundwork to understand exactly how this compound interacts with living cells.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward 10-epi-gamma-Eudesmol having properties that may support the body's defense against microbial threats.
structure_function.basis: This rests on six papers, including animal and laboratory studies evaluating its anti-infective potential.

structure_function.statement: This molecule is being studied for its potential to support cellular health by acting as an antioxidant.
structure_function.basis: Five papers, primarily animal and in vitro research, have explored its ability to neutralize oxidative stress.

structure_function.statement: Early animal work points toward a potential role in supporting healthy inflammatory responses.
structure_function.basis: This is based on three animal studies investigating its effects on inflammation.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether 10-epi-gamma-Eudesmol can effectively inhibit bacterial or fungal growth in living systems, which could eventually point to new natural anti-infective applications.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A Phase 1 human safety and dosing trial applying a standardized topical formulation of 10-epi-gamma-Eudesmol to healthy volunteers to measure skin microbiome changes and tolerability over two weeks.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward this molecule helping to modulate inflammatory pathways, raising the question of whether it could soothe tissue irritation in humans.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human trial measuring systemic inflammatory markers like CRP in healthy adults taking a standardized oral dose over 30 days.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating if the properties observed in early models mean this compound could one day play a role in targeted cellular therapies.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A Phase 1 human clinical trial evaluating the safety, maximum tolerated dose, and pharmacokinetic profile of an isolated 10-epi-gamma-Eudesmol therapeutic in healthy volunteers over a 4-week period.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is animal research (Oxford level 5); the rest of the literature consists of laboratory studies and chemical profiling.
